local_facts.claim: Pennsylvania drivers may select limited tort or full tort. The Pennsylvania Insurance Department explains that limited tort preserves recovery of out-of-pocket medical and other expenses but limits certain damages, such as pain and suffering, unless an exception applies; full tort retains unrestricted rights to bring suit against a negligent party.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The election on the injured person's own auto policy can change the damages analysis after a Harrisburg collision. The declarations page should be preserved with the crash and medical records before anyone discusses a final release.
local_facts.title: The tort choice on your own policy can shape an injury claim

local_facts.claim: The Dauphin County Court of Common Pleas is located in the Dauphin County Courthouse at 101 Market Street in Harrisburg. Dauphin County says civil matters are submitted by the Prothonotary's Office to Civil, Family and Orphans' Court Administration for review and assignment to a judge.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An insurer claim is not the same as a civil case. If a crash claim requires a filing, the local court has a specific courthouse, filing office, and assignment process that should be understood before a deadline becomes urgent.
local_facts.title: Civil cases have a local filing path at the Dauphin County Courthouse

local_facts.claim: PennDOT's Dauphin County Crash Statistics workbook records 2,914 total crashes in Dauphin County in 2024.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A countywide figure cannot determine fault in any one wreck, but it is a reminder to preserve the report, photographs, witness information, medical records, and insurance papers while the evidence for a specific collision is still available.
local_facts.title: Dauphin County recorded 2,914 crashes in 2024

pricing.table_head: What Pennsylvania law fixes for a Dauphin County crash claim, and what it leaves open

anchors.label: Ceiling on an auto injury fee percentage
anchors.detail: Pennsylvania's conduct rule prohibits an illegal or clearly excessive fee and gives eight measuring factors. No percentage appears anywhere in it.

anchors.label: Workers' compensation counsel fee limit
anchors.detail: The one hard number in Pennsylvania fee law: a judge may approve counsel fees only up to a fifth of the award or of a compromise and release settlement.

anchors.label: District court cost, claim of $4,001 to $12,000
anchors.detail: The 2026 statutory cost for a civil case before a magisterial district judge, the court that hears smaller Dauphin County claims. Postage is extra.

anchors.label: Medical benefit every auto policy must carry
anchors.detail: The statutory floor for first-party medical coverage in Pennsylvania, which is what pays early treatment before any liability claim resolves.

fee_rows.stage: Percentage taken from a crash recovery
fee_rows.note: Judged against eight factors: fixed or contingent, difficulty, preclusion of other work, local custom, amount and result, deadlines, relationship, ability.
The agreement states percentages and expense treatment; at the end the lawyer owes a written statement showing the outcome and the remittance.

fee_rows.stage: Work injury claim instead of a liability claim
fee_rows.note: Counsel fees need judge approval and cannot exceed a fifth of the award, or a fifth of a compromise and release settlement amount.

fee_rows.stage: Cost of starting a small civil case
fee_rows.note: Four 2026 tiers before a magisterial district judge, set by claim size from $500 or less up to the $12,000 limit.
The 2026 statutory cost of an order of execution in that court, with $23 more for an objection to levy.
